newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea seen intervening to support won.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea seen intervening to support won.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea was seen stepping into the won/dollar interbank market early Friday to support the won when it fell to a level of 844.50, dealers said.
Shortly after the intervention the won was trading at 843.70, up from an opening of 844.40.
"We saw the central bank step in at around 844.50 to boost the won against dollar," said a local bank dealer.
Traders have said the won was being pressured by heavy import settlements.
The local dealer said the won/dollar was expected to move sideways for the time being.
